item.title: Gang wars in Georgia: ‘thieves-in-law’ declare vendetta against former chief prosecutor
item.description: How did Georgia’s authorities become caught up in a mafia clan war — and what really lies behind the killing of Levan Jangveladze?

item.title: ‘Have you tried cutting costs?’ Opinion on how Abkhazia could overcome its energy crisis
item.description: The Abkhazian Analytical Centre argues that Abkhazia should adopt a law on energy efficiency and energy saving.

item.title: Graduates of world’s top 50 universities to be exempted from military service in Armenia
item.description: The measure applies to universities included in the Shanghai Ranking. Another mandatory condition requires graduates to work in Armenia for at least three years after completing their studies, in positions assigned by the government.

item.title: Russia is preparing cruises from occupied Ukrainian Mariupol to Batumi in Georgia
item.description: This initiative comes across as a symbolic and political message from Russia amid the war it is waging in Ukraine

item.title: Could Azerbaijan join Trump-initiated ‘Board of Peace’ for Gaza?
item.description: Azerbaijan is neither joining the initiative nor openly opposing it. As before, Baku is adopting a wait-and-see approach.

item.title: New travel rules for Russian minors: how will they affect Abkhazia’s citizens?
item.description: From 20 January, Russian citizens under the age of 14 must have an international passport in order to leave the country.

item.title: Russian journalist on trial over remark that ‘20% of Georgia is occupied by Russia’
item.description: This is the first case in which charges under Russia’s “discrediting the army” law are not related to the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Political prisoners excluded from list of those pardoned in Georgia
item.description: In total, Mikheil Kavelashvili pardoned 159 people to mark the Epiphany holiday.

item.title: ‘Military escalation unlikely, but risks remain’ — Armenian Foreign Intelligence Service report
item.description: Armenia’s Foreign Intelligence Service sees risks in Azerbaijan’s rising military spending and in Baku’s promotion of a narrative about the “return of Western Azerbaijanis” to Armenian territory. This forms part of the service’s outlook for 2026.
